source.title: Information-Theoretic Progress Measures reveal Grokking is an Emergent Phase Transition
source.authors: Kenzo Clauw; S. Stramaglia; D. Marinazzo

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines grokking in a modular-arithmetic toy network. Its training-accuracy figures are related to training error, but it does not test the listed claim versions about CIFAR benchmarks, spurious minima, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy plots for weight-decay and initialization settings. These are related to training error but do not test a listed version. The paper's central synergy and redundancy measures concern grokking dynamics, not the training-error outcomes named in the versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures grokking, generalization and neuronal synergy in a shallow fully connected modular-addition network. It does not test any listed version. Its initialization experiments concern delayed generalization under weight scaling and a constrained norm, without testing activation-matched initialization, signal propagation or trainable depth. Edge-of-stability connections are proposed as future work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret higher-order synergy and redundancy as revealing phases of grokking, suggest that early synergy peaks could predict it, and present preliminary subnetwork evidence concerning generalization. They acknowledge that broader experiments and statistical tests are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a two-layer fully connected ReLU network on modular addition using full-batch AdamW; it does not use the listed claim recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight decay and initialization settings are varied; the authors report that very high weight decay and initialization settings do not achieve grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 8 and 9 report training-accuracy curves across weight-decay and initialization settings in a shallow modular-addition network; curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay and initialization scaling affect training dynamics in shallow modular-addition networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report delayed generalization and early synergy peaks for selected settings, with no grokking at excessive weight decay or unsuitable initialization scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early neuronal synergy peaks may predict grokking under the tested modular-addition recipes.

record.problems: The authors describe the model and benchmark as simple and note that scaling width and depth remains future work. The training-accuracy results appear only in plots, without stated numeric values or uncertainty for those outcomes.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks fitting CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and dependence on size, stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student realizability, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature reduction, recovery, divergence and sustained edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Failure to grok is not evidence of substantial training error. Claims about loss geometry are hypotheses here, rather than measured curvature or demonstrated spurious local minima. The supplied figure text contains axes and legends but does not preserve curve trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; model size, optimizer, and stopping conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, batch normalization, plain tanh networks, and Fixup residual networks.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual networks.
